spans.text: On the outskirts of Frankfurt, White Zone.
Oh... oh!
Kalina, come take a look! Quick!
Hearing Six12 over the channel, Kalina and Tokarev slip past the guards and hurry to her side.
Following Six12's pointing finger, Kalina notices something strange in the corner of a wall.
Oh? This looks kind of familiar...
Yeah. It feels like I've seen it somewhere before.
One, two, three...
...These are battlefield codes only Griffin Dolls would use!
...Miss Kalina, look! There are more over here!
Mm. The markings are still fresh. They were probably carved within the last couple of days.
The scratches on the ground look random at first... but if you trace them toward seven o'clock, you'll notice they're more densely distributed in that direction.
That can't just be my imagination.
Kalina follows the direction Tokarev indicates. Just as she says, those markings—each bearing a distinctive, familiar style—form a route marker, subtle yet deliberate.
And as for who left them...
Kalina meets Tokarev's gaze, delight blooming across her face.
It's the Commander!
Yes! It has to be. As long as we follow these markings, we'll definitely find where the Commander is.
Kalina signals the team members who had split up to regroup at their location.
Tokarev takes point, scouting ahead and identifying the markings, while Kalina and the others secure the team's safety and erase their tracks as they move.
Following the trail, Kalina's group arrives at an abandoned transport station.
It's four kilometers from where the medical supply vehicle was ditched, far from the site of investigation.
Whoa... the Commander isn't hiding around here, are they?
This place is a mess.
It is messy, but it's also extremely well-concealed. It's far from the site of investigation and convenient for carrying medical supplies.
Given that the Commander is injured, this location is both hidden and secure enough.
I get that, but... there are weeds growing everywhere, and everything's rusted to hell. Where are we even supposed to look for the Commander's markings?
That last one we found earlier—wasn't that the final sign?
CZ-805 isn't wrong. The area is a wreck. Rusted loading equipment lies abandoned among warehouses that have long since collapsed and caved in.
Some shipping containers have had their paint eaten away by wind and rain, exposing brittle rust beneath. Six12 pokes one lightly with her finger, and a chunk breaks off.
Kalina takes it all in.
Everyone, split up and search. You know the drill. Stay alert.
The others nod. As escort, Tokarev stays close by Kalina's side.
Once inside the transport station, Kalina feels that even spotting a shell crater nearby would be difficult, let alone signs of where the Commander might be hiding.
With so much visual noise, any clue is swallowed up.
Miss Kalina? You've seemed off for a while now. What's on your mind?
I'm thinking about what the Commander is really trying to do.
These markings can only be deciphered by those from Griffin. If they're a code that the Commander left behind, that part is easy enough to understand.
The problem is... when you look at the bigger picture, something doesn't add up.
Bigger picture...?
I don't quite follow.
First, the location where the GPS signal vanished. As you said, that was carefully chosen.
At first, I thought your analysis was a stretch, but the medical supply vehicle changed my mind.
The medical supply vehicle?
Yes. The Commander seized it, then abandoned it there.
From the list of stolen medications, it's clear that the Commander was badly injured.

If the purpose of seizing the vehicle was treatment, the timing doesn't work—they wouldn't have enough time to administer comprehensive treatment within the time between stealing and abandoning the vehicle.
If abandoning the vehicle was meant to hide their tracks, then taking the vehicle in the first place was far too conspicuous...
And really, was it even necessary to take the whole vehicle? The Commander should have taken only the medicine they needed...
And then there are these markings...
At first, there were many of them, but the farther we follow the trail, the fewer there are...
Have you noticed the pattern?
It feels like... the Commander keeps leaving clues, but then cutting them off...
As if they want to tell us where they are, but deliberately keep us at a distance?
You're mostly right, but it's not about distance...
It's about getting the timing right.
Timing...?
Yes. Think about it.
Even though the clues are encoded so that only we can read them, the markings themselves are extremely conspicuous.
It's like dropping your bankbook on the street—anyone who finds it knows someone lost money, but without the password, they can't withdraw a thing.
So even if they can't access it... they still know someone lost something?
Exactly...

Like you, I can't quite grasp the Commander's true intention... Leaving clues only Griffin folks can read, stealing medication that perfectly matches the medical plan I prepared... it's as if they knew I would come?
It feels like... flying a kite. Just when it's about to rise higher, the string is cut at the last second.
Miss Kalina, don't lose heart. Even if things are really as you say, then we are still getting closer to the Commander.
In other words, this is just a small stretch of darkness before dawn...
None of our efforts have been in vain. We've been through situations like this far too many times already.
If anything, it's the opposite—
"If every problem could be solved easily, there must be a carefully crafted lie behind it all."
Isn't that right?
They speak in unison, perfectly in sync.
Tokarev is a bit taken aback. Seeing her expression, Kalina can't help but laugh.
Haha... looks like you remembered that line.
I suppose it's quite apt, considering the situation. As long as we keep going to the very end, everything will become clear.
It's wonderful, Miss Kalina.
Hm? What is?
It's... truly wonderful to see you smile again.
How strange. I owe much to both the Commander and you.
Without your support, I wouldn't have made it this far.
It's my duty. You don't need to—
Huh?! Look over there!
Even while chatting, neither of them has let their eyes stray from the ground for a single moment.
Tokarev is the first to spot the anomaly. Following her gaze, Kalina sees the final marking.
This direction leads to...
Having figured out the direction, Kalina breaks into a run. Tokarev follows close behind.
They run a short distance farther, reaching the most remote corner of the transport station.
There, Kalina carefully examines a patch of ground strewn with debris.
This is...
This is a ventilation shaft! And look! The cover looks like it's been pried open with a crowbar!
We're... getting closer to the Commander again...
Mm... this should be it. Call everyone over. We'll regroup here.
Got it!
Before long, the other three Dolls arrive.
The metal cover of the ventilation shaft is heavy, and it takes all of them working together to pry it open.
Once the opening is wide enough for a person to fit through, Kalina peers down.
Below, the shaft drops into darkness, with a passage leading deeper underground.
Looks like we've found the right place.
We'll go down one by one. Six12 first, Tokarev second, CZ-805 with the assault rifle behind me, and C14 bringing up the rear.
Understood!
Kalina assigns the order based on the Dolls' weapon type. After they descend in sequence, C14 carefully replaces the shaft cover, restoring it to its original state.
